I noticed that Miss Nadia was very open about recording people. She would ask for people's permission beforehand for their consent to record them and then she would straight up start recording 6-second clips of each person right up in their face with no shyness. This taught me that when you're doing work and you have the permission to do said work from people that you're recording, you should really try your best to deliver the best product even if it's uncomfortable in your eyes.

Another thing that I learned was diplomacy with the people that I am working with or recording. In my first week, I was assigned to work with Dr. Hisham Soleiman, but unfortunately things didn't pan out. However, I did meet him again in this gathering of industry professionals and I shook his hand and made sure everything between us was okay. This taught me that being polite and diplomatic despite potential negative experiences is important to sustain good relationships for human decency and the sanctity of future projects.

* Recorded and prepped footage (encoded and labelled)   
* Edited first draft of Open Day video 

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

**2\. Significant Moments of Learning (Challenges, Decisions, or Problems Encountered)**

*(Identify one or two moments that taught you something important.)*  
Example prompts:

* What decision did you make?   
* What did you notice during a task or meeting?  
* What surprised you?

This week was tough. I had to record back-to-back essentially for three days. The open day video taught me that some shoots will take a lot longer.

I was told to give a full overview of the entire event, so that's what I did. I covered everything from the beginning till the end, and I recorded everything. I had problems, majority technical problems, because I had to record my phone, and my phone has very limited storage. I had to keep pulling out my laptop and transferring files and recording some more and then doing that over and over again, but I got through, even though I was incredibly tired.

The day of the open day, I still locked in and did my work and tried my best and recorded everything I possibly could have. It took about six hours, this whole process, but it was fun as much as it was exhausting.

I recorded footage of all the faculties of FCMM, of the auditorium event of the tour. Unfortunately, not Mascomm's tour, because I could not find them, so I took footage from Nadia for that, then photos of people going home. 

I was very surprised by how people look at you when you're recording and how you kind of actually have to ignore them. People are very confused as to why this guy is recording everything, and some people did ask me. I told them honestly what I was doing, and they wished me luck, so communication is important. You should communicate with the people that you're recording, and I learned to do that. 

For the filming and IMC discussions, I did go and film, and it was very fun as well, but it was also awkward having to get in the face of my peers to record them. I've had people ask me to not include them in the footage and not record them all together, and of course I respected their wishes because consent is important. I continued to ignore how people were looking at me and just did my work as I was supposed to.

*(Brief, factual overview)*

*This week, I took feedback from Nadia and made the final version of the Open Day video. I edited the IMC and filming discussions.* 

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

**2\. Significant Moments of Learning (Challenges, Decisions, or Problems Encountered)**

*(Identify one or two moments that taught you something important.)*  
Example prompts:

* What decision did you make?   
* What did you notice during a task or meeting?  
* What surprised you?

This week I learned that editing is hard. Editing is really, really, really hard. Why is that? Because it takes a lot of time. In order to do a good edit, you need to:

* find a trending audio so that your video stays relevant  
* time your clips to the beat of that audio so that it feels holistic and easy to watch  
* record a voiceover, so you have to write a script as well  
* record the voiceover process, the audio, and then put it in the timeline  
* cut that up as well  
* captions. Oh my god, captions. You have to create captions for your video in case someone's not listening, because a lot of people use TikTok with their sound off in public places and such

Of course, dealing with the editing software itself (Premiere and Cap Cut) both have their strengths and weaknesses. Premiere is really good at fine detail, so I use that for open day, but for quick edits I used Cap Cut for the speed of it. I was surprised by how much time it took, genuinely, to edit. It's like I was figuratively ripping my hair out looking at the screen, trying to figure out how I'm going to do this on time. I did eventually do it, but it was a struggle. 

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

Consider: Why was this moment important? What did it reveal about your skills or assumptions? How does it relate to professional standards or industry expectations?

*(Apply one academic idea or industry principle.)* Examples: Audience engagement, accuracy & verification, etc. *(Include in-text citation if possible.)*

This moment revealed to me that I am capable of problem-solving and building an edit that looks clean and respectable while keeping engagement high. It was not easy, and I did learn a lot about how to write a TikTok script and how to edit a TikTok video. I am really proud of the output that I gave. I believe it relates to professional standards in that you have to start somewhere. You cannot become a professional without learning how to do something first, so you have to be kind to yourself and learn, but also give the best output you possibly can.
